history: From the Café Royal Cocktail Book, 1937. The name refers to twisting the lion’s tail: doing something dangerous, in this case drinking bourbon at a British hotel bar.
whyItWorks: Allspice dram is baking spice in liquid form; against lime rather than lemon it stays sharp instead of turning into mulled cider.
steps: Shake all liquid ingredients with ice.
Express a lime twist over the top.
techniqueNotes: Allspice dram is potent—half an ounce is the ceiling before it takes over.
Lime, not lemon. Lemon makes it taste like a hot toddy served cold.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Enough oak to carry the spice.
Softer fruit if the dram is aggressive.

substitutions.notes: Falernum is sweeter and lighter; use ¾ oz and drop the simple syrup.

name: Lion's Tail
description: Bourbon, allspice dram and lime—a spiced whiskey sour from the tail end of the cocktail age.
